Name: Golden Hour Transitions - Customizable Sunset Lighting
Author: ZeroXPatch
Description:
[center][b][size=6]Golden Transitions
[/size][/b]
[i]Experience the magic of the "Golden Hour" with a fully customizable sunset overhaul.

[color=#00ff00]Thanks for the ideas! 
[/color][/i][color=#00ff00]eddystalin and Halibumbum[/color]

Safe to uninstall anytime. Removing it just disables the features.[/center][center][size=4][color=#ffff00]Works perfectly with [b]Dynamic Dusk[/b] to sync the golden glow with your randomized/Realistic sunset times.
[/color]
 [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/40783]Dynamic Dusk - Realistic Night Transition or Randomized[/url]﻿
[/size][/center]

Also perfect with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/41189]Sunrise Transitions - Customizable Morning Atmosphere[/url] (Control sunrise)

[line]

[size=4][b]The Concept[/b][/size]
In vanilla Stardew Valley, the transition from day to night is visually static. Every sunset looks the same, regardless of the season.

[b]Golden Transitions[/b] changes this by adding a stunning, atmospheric overlay that bridges the gap between afternoon and night. Whether you want the deep burning orange of a Summer dusk or the pale, cold yellow of a Winter evening, this mod gives you complete control.

[line]
[center]﻿﻿[/center]﻿

[size=4][b]Key Features[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [b]Full Seasonal Customization[/b]
You are no longer limited to one color. You can now configure unique settings for [b]Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter[/b] individually.* Make Spring sunsets soft and pink.* Make Summer sunsets bright and golden.* Make Winter sunsets pale and short.[*] [b]The "Golden Hour" Effect[/b]
The mod introduces a "Build-Up" phase before the sun actually sets. Watch as your farm slowly begins to glow with warmth in the late afternoon, peaking exactly at sunset.[*] [b]New: Randomized Atmosphere[/b]
Want to shake things up? Enable [b]Random Mode[/b]. [color=#ffff00]The mod will randomly pick one of your 4 Seasonal Presets to use based on your chosen frequency[/color] (Daily, Weekly, or Seasonally).* [i]Example:[/i] You might get a crisp "Winter-style" sunset on a cool Spring evening, or a deep "Fall-style" red glow during Summer.[*] [b]Seamless Integration[/b]
This mod does not force the time; it visualizes it. If you use mods that change when the sun sets (like[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/40783] [b]Dynamic Dusk[/b][/url]), Golden Transitions automatically adapts to match the new sunset time perfectly.[/list]
[b][size=4][color=#00ff00]A graph showing how the Golden Hour effect works:[/color]

[list]
[*][b][size=4][color=#ffff00]5:30pm - 30 mins before sunset, the intensity start climbing[/color][/size][/b]
[*][b][size=4][color=#ffff00]6pm - sunset time, peak of intensity.[/color][/size][/b]
[*][b][size=4][color=#ffff00]8pm - intensity slowly fading away in two hours[/color][/size][/b]
[/list]
Tip: using [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/40783]Dynamic Dusk[/url] you can configure the sunset time, the golden transition will adapt to the new sunset time using the same scheme shown below.

[line]

[size=4][b]Configuration Guide - [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/articles/3988] A guide to how to configure your own[/url]﻿
[/b][/size]
You can tweak every aspect of the sunset using [b]Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM)[/b].

[b]1. Seasonal Profiles[/b]
The menu now has separate sections for Spring, Summer, Fall, and Winter. For each season, you can set:
[list]
[*] [b]RGB Color:[/b] The exact color of the sunset glow.
[*] [b]Intensity:[/b] How strong the glow is (Opacity 0-100%).
[*] [b]Build-Up:[/b] How many minutes [i]before[/i] sunset the glow begins.
[*] [b]Fade-Out:[/b] How many minutes [i]after[/i] sunset the glow lingers.
[/list]

[b]2. Randomization Settings[/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Enable Random Mode:[/b]
* [b]OFF (Default):[/b] The mod strictly follows the current game season (e.g., if it is Winter, it uses your Winter settings).* [b]ON:[/b] The mod treats your seasonal settings as "Presets" and picks one randomly.[*] [b]Frequency:[/b]
* [b]Daily:[/b] A different visual style every morning.* [b]Weekly:[/b] The style changes every Monday.* [b]Seasonal:[/b] The style changes on Day 1 of the season.[/list]

[size=4][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]
[list]
[*] Compatible with Stardew Valley 1.6+
[*] Highly recommended for use with [b]Dynamic Dusk[/b] for a fully synchronized, randomized sunset experience.
[*] Compatible with most texture replacements and recolors (overlay renders on top of the world).
[/list]


[center]                    [color=#ffff00][size=6]🎨 Ultimate Configuration Guide for Golden Transitions
[/size][/color][/center]
This mod gives you total control over the sunset atmosphere. Here is how to tweak the settings to get the exact look you want.

1. Mastering the Color (RGB)The color is defined by mixing [b]Red[/b], [b]Green[/b], and [b]Blue[/b].
[list]
[*][b]Range:[/b] 0 (None) to 255 (Max).
[/list][b]The Golden Rule for Sunsets:
[/b]
For a warm sunset, you almost always want [b]Red at 255 (Max)[/b]. You will mostly be adjusting [b]Green[/b] to change the hue.
[list]
[*][b]To make it YELLOW / GOLD:[/b]
[list]
[*]Turn [b]Green UP[/b] (towards 200).
[*]Think: Sunflowers, Noon sun.
[/list][*][b]To make it ORANGE:[/b]
[list]
[*]Set [b]Green to MEDIUM[/b] (around 120).
[*]Think: Typical Stardew sunset.
[/list][*][b]To make it RED / BURNING:[/b]
[list]
[*]Turn [b]Green DOWN[/b] (towards 50).
[*]Think: Deep summer heat, apocalypse, dramatic dusk.
[/list][*][b]To make it PASTEL / PINK:[/b]
[list]
[*]Turn [b]Blue UP[/b] (towards 100+).
[*]Think: Spring twilight, cotton candy clouds.
[/list][/list][line][b]2. Controlling Intensity (Opacity)
[/b]
This setting controls how "solid" the color overlay is. Think of it like putting on a pair of tinted sunglasses.
[list]
[*][b]Low (10% - 25%):[/b] Very subtle. Just a hint of warmth. Best if you want to keep the vanilla lighting visible underneath.
[*][b]Medium (30% - 50%):[/b] [b](Recommended)[/b] The "Sweet Spot." You can see the game world clearly, but the atmosphere is distinct and glowing.
[*][b]High (60% - 80%):[/b] Heavy atmosphere. The screen will be very tinted. Good for dramatic "Burning Red" sunsets, but might make it harder to see forage items.
[*][b]Max (100%):[/b] Solid wall of color. Not recommended for gameplay.
[/list][line][b]3. Understanding the Timeline
[/b]
The mod splits the sunset into two phases based on the "Sunset Time" (e.g., 6:00 PM).
Phase A: Build-Up (Before Sunset)This is the [b]"Golden Hour."[/b] It controls how early the glow starts appearing.
[list]
[*][b]Setting:[/b] Build-Up Duration (Minutes)
[*][b]Example (45 Mins):[/b] If sunset is at 6:00 PM, the glow starts fading in at [b]5:15 PM[/b].
[*][b]Usage:[/b]
[list]
[*]Set to [b]60+[/b] for a long, lazy afternoon glow.
[*]Set to [b]0[/b] if you want the sky to stay normal until the exact moment of sunset.
[/list][/list]Phase B: Fade-Out (After Sunset)
This is the [b]"Twilight / Afterglow."[/b] It controls how long the color lingers while the sky turns dark.
[list]
[*][b]Setting:[/b] Fade-Out Duration (Minutes)
[*][b]Example (120 Mins):[/b] If sunset is at 6:00 PM, the orange glow will slowly fade away until it is gone at [b]8:00 PM[/b].
[*][b]Usage:[/b]
[list]
[*]Set to [b]120[/b] (2 hours) to match the game's natural darkening speed. The orange will disappear exactly when it hits "pitch black."
[*]Set to [b]180+[/b] if you want a "Hazy Night" where the warmth lingers into the darkness.
[/list][/list]
